title: Gradient Descent, From the Loss Up
summary: Build linear regression from the loss up: the MSE cost, its gradient, the update rule, L2 regularization, and how to check a gradient numerically.
takeaways: A model, a loss, its gradient and an update rule make up nearly every training loop.
Gradient descent steps against the gradient. The learning rate sets the step size.
With a sensible learning rate the cost never increases, which makes a great debugging signal.
Ridge (L2) adds (λ/2m)·‖w‖² and shrinks weights, but never the bias.

steps.label: Predict
steps.detail: ŷ = X @ w + b for every example at once.

steps.label: Residual
steps.detail: r = ŷ − y, the error for each example.

steps.label: Update
steps.detail: w ← w − α·∂J/∂w and b ← b − α·∂J/∂b, both computed at the same point.

terms.definition: The average of squared prediction errors; the standard regression loss.
The vector of partial derivatives, pointing in the direction of steepest increase of a function.
The step size α used in gradient descent updates.
Adding a penalty proportional to ‖w‖² to the loss to discourage large weights (ridge regression).
Approximating a derivative as [J(w+ε) − J(w−ε)] / 2ε to verify an analytic gradient.
